os_macos_intro: Download the app, drag it to Applications and the rest happens in your browser. AI Detector runs entirely on your own Mac — no subscription, no cloud.
os_macos_download_desc: Download the macOS file from the latest release.
os_macos_req_text: You need a Mac with Apple Silicon (M1, M2, M3, M4 or newer) and macOS 14 Sonoma or newer. Detection runs on the Neural Engine of the chip: fast, quiet and very energy-efficient.
os_hw_apple_silicon: Mac with Apple Silicon (M1 or newer), macOS 14+
os_note_text: Macs with an Intel processor are not supported.
os_macos_step1_1: Open the releases page with the button above, or search Google for “ESchouten ai-detector” and click Releases on GitHub.
os_macos_step1_2: Under Assets of the latest release, click AI-Detector-<version>-macos-arm64.dmg. The file is saved in your Downloads folder.
os_macos_step1_caption: The latest release on GitHub: the macOS file (.dmg) is listed under Assets.
os_macos_step2_1: Double-click the .dmg file in Downloads. A window opens with the AI Detector icon.
os_macos_step2_3: Eject the disk image in Finder and delete the .dmg file — it is no longer needed.
os_macos_step3_title: Give the Mac permission to open the app
os_macos_step3_intro: AI Detector does not come from the App Store and has no paid Apple developer certificate, so macOS blocks it the first time — with a message such as “cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified” or “is damaged and can’t be opened”. Pick one of the methods below.
os_macos_step3_a_1: Open AI Detector once from Applications and click Done or Cancel on the security message.
os_macos_step3_a_2: Click the Apple logo at the top left and open System Settings → Privacy & Security.
os_macos_step3_a_3: Scroll down to Security. You see a line saying that “AI Detector” was blocked.
os_macos_step3_a_4: Click Open Anyway, confirm with your Mac password or Touch ID and click Open. From now on the app opens without warnings.
os_macos_step3_b_2: Hold Control and click AI Detector (or right-click it), then choose Open.
os_macos_step3_b_3: Click Open in the dialog. macOS remembers this choice.
os_macos_step3_c_title: Method C — via Terminal (if macOS says the app is “damaged”)
os_macos_step3_c_intro: macOS sometimes puts downloaded apps in quarantine. You remove that mark with one command:
os_macos_step3_c_1: Open Terminal (press Cmd + Space, type Terminal and press Enter).
os_macos_step3_c_2: Paste the command below and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>. Asked for a password? Type your Mac login password — you see no characters while typing, that is normal.
os_macos_keep_1: Use a network cable. Connect the Mac and the cameras with a wired connection. No ethernet port on your MacBook or Mac mini? Use a reliable USB-C to ethernet adapter.
os_macos_keep_2: No sleep settings needed. While monitoring is on, AI Detector keeps the Mac awake by itself. A MacBook still sleeps when you close the lid, so leave it open.
os_macos_keep_3: Start at login and updates. In the AI Detector menu in the menu bar (top right) you can switch on Open at login and choose Check for Updates.
